the memory term, in some cases, can not produce a decay rate of the energy, and the decay rate is controlled by a number that is independent of the initial data.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the decay rate of solution of the Cauchy problems for the Bresse system coupled to heat equation.
the study of the decay properties of solutions of the one-dimensional Bress system with Gurting–Pipkin heat conduction.

the study of the decay properties of solutions of the Cauchy Problem for the one-dimensional linear Bresse system coupled to the Gurtin-Pikin heat conduction law, and we provide some new results on the decay properties of such system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the decay rate of a solution of the Cauchy Problem for the Bresse system coupled by Gurtin– Pipkin heat conduction law, depends on the strength of the frictional and memory dissipative terms, the regularity of the initial data and on the number of derivatives of the solution.
the memory term in the Bresse system is very weak, and it cannot produce a decay rate of solutions.

, in the presence of a frictional term, the solution decays at an exponential rate and this rate is determined by a parameter that depends on the frictional coefficient, the memory coefficient and the heat conduction parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decay rate of a solution of the Cauchy problems is very sensitive to the parameters of the problem and the regularity of the initial data.
, in the presence of the frictional term, the decay rate is faster than the one induced by the Gurting–Pipkin term.

we have proved that the decay rate of a solution of the Cauchy problems for the Bresse system coupled to the Gurtin-Pikpin heat conduction depends on both the memory and friction damping coefficients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the presence of the frictional term, the decay rates of the solution are independent of the strength of the memory term.
, the Gurtin-Pikin thermal law does not produce a decay rate in the absence of frictional damping.
the Gurtin-Pikpin heat law does not induce enough dissipation to produce decay rates of the solution.
